subject: Day 82: laugh-and-narrate outing
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi laughs reliably now and settles visibly when a familiar voice enters the room. Combine that reciprocity with outdoor time: a calm walk where you play for laughs and narrate what he watches turns one outing into motor, social, and language input at once.

Action items
- Take a 20-30 minute walk in daylight and play for laughs along the way. Sunlight aids the parent's cardiovascular recovery and varies his sensory input, though it does not replace the 400 IU daily vitamin D he still needs as a breastfed or predominantly breastfed infant. AAP vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Trade laughs and exaggerated faces during the walk and on his back at home. Reliable laughing and clear preference for familiar people are right on schedule for the end of the quarter. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Plan for the first childcare illness, which usually arrives within two to four weeks of starting. Have the pediatrician's after-hours line saved and decide in advance who stays home.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Profuse drooling and hand-sucking. This reflects salivary gland maturation, not teething; first teeth typically arrive at 6-10 months.
- [monitor] No social smile or no reciprocal laugh by now. It is usually nothing, but note it so you can raise it at the 4-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Vomiting that persists beyond 24 hours, or refusal of several feeds in a row.
- [call now] Fever of 100.4F rectal or higher under 90 days, seizure-like activity, or a color change during a feed. Call same-day; if his lips go blue, call 911!

Enrichment opportunities
- Narrate what he is looking at during the walk in full sentences, naming what catches his eye. Conversational turns built on his attention, not raw word count, are what predict later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Run several short serve-and-return rounds: respond to his coo as if he spoke, pause two to three seconds, then answer his next sound. The back-and-forth is the active ingredient even before words. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Give him outdoor tactile contrast on the same outing, letting him feel a blanket on grass or watch leaves move, to widen his sensory range beyond the indoor palette.

Upcoming
- Day 84-91 (~3 months): sleep-consolidation window opens; lock in a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (~4 months): 4-month well visit with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.
- Day 98-126 (~14-18 weeks): 4-month sleep regression typically begins.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
